static_traits.name: Ming Kai
static_traits.social_status: With colleagues: distant since the incident; social support: has a few close friends to confide in, but has not yet discussed this incident with them.
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems appeared before; no psychotherapy or counseling received; no major physical illness.
static_traits.language_features: Tense but willing to seek help and cooperate; clear expression, fairly good logic; able to reflect and self-examine; self-critical tendencies; speech rate and language style not mentioned.

basic_info.main_problem: Because I messed up a customer's order at work today, I feel I am a terrible employee, producing a sense of incompetence and self-blame, and I keep replaying the mistake.
basic_info.core_demands: This work incident triggered strong negative emotions and self-criticism; hoping to cope with and alleviate these feelings through counseling.

special_situations.event: At work, gets a customer's order wrong, is discovered by the manager and corrected on the spot
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake at work, it means I am incompetent and not suited for this job
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing oneself to be more careful, repeatedly checking orders to avoid making mistakes again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a terrible employee

special_situations.event: The manager did not say much, with a serious expression, quickly handling the mistake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a supervisor gives no positive feedback or seems unhappy, it means they are disappointed in me and deem me incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeping distance from colleagues to avoid being evaluated; avoiding communicating with the manager
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She must think I am incompetent, I disappointed her

special_situations.event: Afterwards constantly recalling this mistake, ignoring my own good performance at work in the past
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One mistake is enough to negate my past competence and performance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continually focuses on mistake details to remind oneself to avoid repeating them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This mistake shows I'm no good

special_situations.event: Thinking about continuing to interact with customers or going to work again in the future
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Making this mistake means I will constantly make mistakes in the future and disappoint everyone
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Overly cautious, repeatedly double-checks to try to prevent all mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will keep making mistakes and disappoint everyone

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized by superiors and colleagues, seen as competent, and accepted
core_conflict.fear: Fearing criticism, being seen as incompetent, being rejected or losing trust
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being judged by keeping distance from colleagues
Maintains control and a sense of safety through self-criticism and excessive caution

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a mistake-prone employee
object_relations.object_representation: The silent manager who may be disappointed and judgmental

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the manager corrects the order on the spot without stating a position clearly, or facing others' silence/serious expressions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting the other's silence as disappointment in oneself, believing oneself seen as incompetent (transference: Projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: With a gentle and respectful tone, first validate the client's feelings, then use open-ended questioning to distinguish feelings from evidence, inviting generating other possible explanations; avoiding judgment and confrontation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When repeatedly recalling mistakes and experiencing intense shame
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning the disappointment/anger that should point at the situation against the self, believing 'it is all my fault'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a supportive and empathic tone; helping distinguish external from internal responsibility boundaries; encouraging self-compassion and feasible improvement plans, reducing self-punishment.

manifestations: Keeping distance from colleagues since the incident
Not yet confiding this incident to close friends
Feels isolated from others in work settings

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently blames oneself and labels oneself ('I am a bad employee')
Overly cautious at work, checks repeatedly to avoid making mistakes again
Worrying about being evaluated and repressing true feelings

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward others or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, turning inward to do it to themselves, i.e. the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Keeping distance from coworkers, not actively communicating or asking for help
Turning worry about and dissatisfaction with the manager into self-criticism and shame
Bearing the pressure alone without discussing the incident with friends

positive_force: Usually works conscientiously and carefully, with few mistakes (has basic job competence and strategies)
Willing to seek help and participate in counseling, able to reflect on one's own thinking patterns
Has a certain degree of social support (has several close friends)
Can consider multiple possible explanations, open to evidence and feedback
negative_force: Tendencies toward catastrophizing and all-or-nothing thinking
Mind-reading and predicting the future leading to excessive worry
Distances himself from colleagues out of fear of being judged, reducing external support
Fear of being criticized affects work performance and emotions

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive self-blame and negating oneself (equating one mistake with incompetence)
antecedent: Thinking about the work mistakes of the day
Seeing the manager correct the order on the spot without giving a clear evaluation
When interacting with customers or preparing for work
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, and mind reading; fear of criticism and shame drive self-punishing thinking
target_behavior.function: Avoids the risk of negative evaluation by others; gains a sense of control through self-punishment
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and anxiety; work performance affected; continuously ruminating on the mistake, declining self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Keeping distance from colleagues; avoiding communication and asking for help
antecedent: Shifts and rest time after a mistake occurs at work
Worrying about being seen as incompetent or disappointing the manager
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and personalization tendency, interprets others' possible reactions as negative evaluations of oneself
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the potential discomfort of being evaluated and criticized
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased interpersonal support, increased loneliness; anxiety and self-doubt maintained or even intensified
